subtitle: How horses, cotton and a god-marked coin tied a hill kingdom to the sea

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a bustling Konkan harbour fading into the hill-fort of Devagiri in the distance
panels.action: Konkan Varaha-Merchant stands at a busy quay stacked with bales and amphorae, holding up a gleaming Yadava varaha coin as ships ride in the surf and, far inland, Devagiri’s rocky silhouette rises under a hazy sun.

dialogue.text: Between Devagiri’s stone and the Konkan’s surf, merchants, horses and a small silver coin bound the Yadava kingdom to the wide sea-road of the world.

i18n.hi: देवगिरि की चट्टान और कोंकण की लहरों के बीच, साहूकार, घोड़े और एक छोटा चाँदी का सिक्का यादवों को दुनिया की बड़ी समुद्री राह से बाँधता था।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye of the Deccan plateau sloping down to the western sea
panels.action: A sweeping view shows Devagiri fort on its basalt hill, fields and towns scattered across the Deccan plain, then the land breaking into green Ghats that drop towards the shimmering line of the Arabian Sea.

dialogue.text: The Yadavas of Devagiri ruled from rock and plateau, but their fortunes flowed along two roads: the brown cart-tracks of the Deccan and the blue sea-lanes of the Konkan coast.

i18n.hi: देवगिरि के यादव चट्टानों से राज करते थे, पर उनकी किस्मत दो राहों पर चलती थी – दक्खन की मिट्टीली बैलगाड़ी पगडंडियाँ और कोंकण की नीली समुद्री लकीरें।

panels.shot: mid-wide of irrigated fields and village granaries under a hot sky
panels.action: Farmers thresh grain beside mud-plastered granaries; bundles of cotton lie in the shade, bullock carts creak along a dusty track leading toward the distant escarpment of the Western Ghats.

dialogue.text: Fields of grain and plots of cotton covered the Deccan plain. Their surplus, drawn as tax and tribute, fed both temples and armies, and made trade caravans worth the dust and danger.

i18n.hi: दक्खन के मैदान में अनाज के खेत और कपास की क्यारियाँ फैली थीं। उनका बचा हिस्सा, कर और नज़राने में खिंचकर, मंदिरों और सेनाओं को पलता था और कारवाँ को धूल और ख़तरे लायक बनाता था।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on loaded bullock cart wheels rolling over stones
panels.action: A heavy bullock cart laden with sacks of grain and tightly wrapped cotton bales jolts down a rocky slope; Konkan Varaha-Merchant walks beside it, cloth-wrapped ledger at his waist, eyes on the twisting path.

dialogue.text: Merchants moved this wealth from village to town, from Deccan markets to passes in the Ghats. Their risks were bandits, weather, and toll posts of kings who watched every road.

i18n.hi: साहूकार यह दौलत गाँव से कस्बे, दक्खन के हाटों से घाटों के दर्रों तक ढोते थे। उनका डर था डाकू, मौसम, और उन राजाओं की चुंगियाँ जो हर राह पर नज़र रखते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a steep ghat road with caravans climbing and descending
panels.action: Long lines of pack-oxen and men wind along a narrow ghat road carved into the hillside; mist hangs over deep valleys, and in the middle of the column Konkan Varaha-Merchant pauses, looking down toward a faint glimpse of sea.

dialogue.text: Over the Western Ghats, narrow tracks bound plateau to coast. Down these slopes went cotton, sugar and grain; up them came salt, metal, and something more prized than any bale—warhorses.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी घाट पर सँकरी पगडंडियाँ पठार को किनारे से बाँधती थीं। इन्हीं ढलानों से कपास, गुड़ और अनाज उतरता; ऊपर चढ़कर आता नमक, धातु, और सबसे कीमती बोझ – जंगी घोड़े।

panels.shot: sweeping harbour-wide of Thane or Chaul filled with dhows and local craft
panels.action: At a bustling Konkan port, broad-beamed dhows with stitched sails anchor offshore while smaller boats ferry goods; Konkan Varaha-Merchant oversees laborers stacking cotton bales near piles of imported jars and rolled carpets.

dialogue.text: On the Konkan shore, ports like Thane, Chaul and Sopara faced the Arabian Sea. From here, men of many tongues followed the monsoon winds to Gujarat, Hormuz and beyond.

i18n.hi: कोंकण के तट पर ठाणे, चौल, सोपारा जैसे बंदरगाह अरबी सागर की ओर मुख किए थे। यहीं से कई ज़बानें बोलने वाले लोग मानसून के सहारे गुजरात, होर्मुज़ और आगे बढ़ते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot at eye level of foreign merchants and Indian traders negotiating on the quay
panels.action: Bearded merchants in long robes and turbans from the Gulf stand opposite Konkan Varaha-Merchant and other local traders, gesturing over ledgers and samples of textiles while horses on a nearby vessel nicker unseen.

dialogue.text: Ranabir Chakravarti traces how foreign traders brought horses from the Persian Gulf to these creeks, exchanging them for Indian textiles, spices and money raised inland.

i18n.hi: रणबीर चक्रवर्ती बताते हैं कैसे परदेशी व्यापारी फारस की खाड़ी से घोड़े इन खाड़ियों तक लाते, और बदले में भारतीय कपड़ा, मसाले और भीतर के इलाकों से आया धन लेते।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of horses being led down from a ship’s gangplank
panels.action: Strong, nervous horses with foreign saddles are led carefully down a wooden gangplank onto the dock, their hooves pounding; Konkan Varaha-Merchant watches, calculating, as handlers struggle to steady them.

dialogue.text: No kingdom of the Deccan could breed enough hardy warhorses. The sea-road brought in mounts from Arabia and Central Asia, vital for cavalry charges and for the prestige of a king’s stables.

i18n.hi: दक्खन का कोई राज्य अपने दम पर इतने मज़बूत जंगी घोड़े नहीं पाल पाता था। समुद्री राह अरब और मध्य एशिया के घोड़े लाती, जो घुड़सवार फ़ौज और राजा के अस्तबल की शान के लिए ज़रूरी थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up of the merchant’s hand counting out coins into another’s palm
panels.action: Konkan Varaha-Merchant’s hand pours neat stacks of small silver and copper coins into the open palm of a horse dealer, while behind them a clerk scratches figures onto a palm-leaf strip.

dialogue.text: Such trade needed trusted money. Under the Yadavas, gold, silver and copper coins passed from royal treasuries into markets, carrying the king’s mark into every bargain and debt.

i18n.hi: ऐसे सौदों के लिए भरोसेमंद पैसा ज़रूरी था। यादव काल में सोने, चाँदी और ताँबे के सिक्के ख़जाने से बाज़ारों तक चलते, और हर सौदे के साथ राजा की मुहर भी घूमती।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a Yadava gold varaha coin held between fingers
panels.action: Between the merchant’s fingers a bright gold varaha coin gleams; its tiny relief shows Varaha, the boar incarnation of Vishnu, advancing, while faint Nagari script curves around the edge.

dialogue.text: In museums today lie Yadava gold varaha or gadyana coins like this, bearing Varaha and legends in script. They remind us that coinage was as much about power and piety as payment.

i18n.hi: आज संग्रहालयों में ऐसे यादव सोने के वराह या गड्याना सिक्के हैं, जिन पर वराह और शिलालेख बने हैं। वे याद दिलाते हैं कि सिक्का सिर्फ़ भुगतान नहीं, सत्ता और भक्ति का निशान भी था।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder mid-shot of the merchant weighing coins on a small balance
panels.action: Konkan Varaha-Merchant sits in a shaded verandah, weighing silver coins in a small balance, separate piles of gold, silver and copper before him as assistants bring in cloth-wrapped bundles.

dialogue.text: Gold varaha were few and heavy, suited to large payments and royal gifts. Silver and copper pieces traveled further, through bazaars and village fairs, sometimes alongside older coins from other dynasties.

i18n.hi: सोने के वराह कम और भारी थे, बड़े भुगतानों और शाही इनामों के लिए ठीक। चाँदी और ताँबे के टुकड़े दूर-दूर तक चले, बाज़ारों और मेलों में, कभी-कभी दूसरी वंशों के पुराने सिक्कों के साथ।

panels.shot: mid-wide interior of a simple guild-like merchants’ hall in a coastal town
panels.action: In a long hall open to the street, several merchants sit together on low platforms, sharing news; Konkan Varaha-Merchant gestures along a map scratched on the floor that links coast to plateau.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions from other Deccan regions speak of merchant groups and guilds. Though specific Yadava records are sparse, traders here too likely formed networks to share risk and bargain with officials.

i18n.hi: दक्खन के और इलाकों के शिलालेखों में व्यापारी जत्थों और श्रेणियों का ज़िक्र है। भले ही यादव लिखत कम मिलती हो, यहाँ के साहूकार भी शायद मिलकर जाल बुनते, ख़तरा बाँटते और अफ़सरों से सौदा करते थे।

panels.shot: high-angle wide of Devagiri’s gates as a caravan arrives with horses and tribute
panels.action: A caravan enters Devagiri’s gate: horses led by grooms, carts of grain and cotton, and chests borne by porters; Konkan Varaha-Merchant walks with them as palace guards watch from the battlements.

dialogue.text: Much of this flow climbed up to Devagiri. Tribute from feudatories, taxes from villages, and profits from coastal trade met on the hill, turning market gains into royal horses and hill-fort defenses.

i18n.hi: इस दौलत का बड़ा हिस्सा आख़िर देवगिरि तक चढ़ आता। जागीरदारों की नज़राने, गाँवों के कर और समुद्री व्यापार के मुनाफ़े इसी पहाड़ी पर मिलकर बाज़ार की कमाई को शाही घोड़ों और किले की दीवारों में बदलते थे।

panels.shot: dim interior wide of a royal treasury hall stacked with chests and tethered horses beyond
panels.action: In a large vaulted hall, wooden chests sit in ordered ranks while, through an archway, a courtyard shows rows of horses tethered under shade; torchlight glints off piled coins in an open chest.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the chronicler Ziauddin Barani described how in 1296, an enemy force seized Devagiri’s wealth and a thousand horses from its stables, evidence of the treasure and cavalry stored here.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद इतिहासकार ज़ियाउद्दीन बरनी ने लिखा कि 1296 में एक दुश्मन फ़ौज ने देवगिरि की दौलत और अस्तबलों से हज़ार घोड़े लूट लिए – यहाँ जमा ख़ज़ाने और घुड़सवार ताक़त की निशानी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Alauddin Khalji’s army approaching Devagiri from the plain (no battle shown)
panels.action: An armed host advances across the plain toward Devagiri’s looming hill, banners snapping; the fort’s outlines stand stark, while smoke from cooking fires rises quietly from the enemy camp below.

dialogue.text: To men like Alauddin Khalji, such stables and treasuries were prizes. Barani’s hostile account shows how the Yadava economy, fed by sea and soil, also painted a target on Devagiri’s rock.

i18n.hi: अलाउद्दीन खिलजी जैसे सेनापतियों के लिए ऐसे अस्तबल और ख़ज़ाने इनाम थे। बरनी की कड़वी कहानी दिखाती है कि समुद्र और ज़मीन से पला यादव आर्थिक जाल ही देवगिरि की चट्टान पर निशाना भी बना।

panels.shot: medium shot of the merchant in a crowd listening to news of Devagiri’s defeat in a coastal bazaar
panels.action: In a crowded coastal market, traders stand stunned as a dusty messenger speaks; Konkan Varaha-Merchant clutches a small pouch of coins, his face shadowed with uncertainty amid the stalls.

dialogue.text: When Devagiri’s fortunes turned, the shock rippled down the ghats. Merchants on the Konkan coast weighed fresh risks, wondering which power would next claim tolls on their roads and coins in their hands.

i18n.hi: जब देवगिरि की किस्मत डगमगाई, तो उसकी गूँज घाटों से नीचे तक उतरी। कोंकण के व्यापारी नए ख़तरों को तौलते रहे, सोचते कि अब किस सत्ता की चुंगी और किसके सिक्के उनके हाथों पर हुक्म चलाएँगे।

panels.shot: close-up of the merchant burying or hiding a small hoard of coins in a niche at home
panels.action: Inside a modest house, Konkan Varaha-Merchant kneels as he seals a small clay jar filled with coins into a wall niche, his fingers pressing wet plaster over it while his family watches silently.

dialogue.text: Some coins vanished into hoards like this, hidden in walls or fields when armies marched. Centuries later, archaeologists and chance diggers would find them, tiny time-capsules of the Yadava economy.

i18n.hi: कुछ सिक्के ऐसे ही ख़ज़ानों में गुम हो गए, दीवारों या खेतों में छिपाकर जब सेनाएँ गुज़रीं। सदियों बाद पुरातत्वविद और किस्मत से खोदने वाले इन्हें पाएँगे – यादव अर्थव्यवस्था की नन्ही समय-डिब्बियाँ।

panels.shot: wide shot of the same harbour years later with subtle signs of changed rule
panels.action: The Konkan harbour bustles again under different banners; Konkan Varaha-Merchant, older now, sits in his booth as sailors unload cargo, new styles of dress and different overlord’s flags marking the passage of regimes.

dialogue.text: Yet the sea-road endured. Even as dynasties rose and fell, Konkan ports kept linking inland fields to ocean routes, and men like our merchant adapted, balancing between new rulers and old habits.

i18n.hi: पर समुद्री राह बनी रही। राजवंश उठे और गिरे, पर कोंकण के बंदरगाह भीतर के खेतों को महासागर से जोड़ते रहे, और हमारे जैसा साहूकार नए राजाओं और पुराने तौर-तरीकों के बीच संतुलन साधता रहा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the varaha coin resting in the merchant’s palm against the backdrop of sea and hills
panels.action: Konkan Varaha-Merchant holds a worn varaha coin in his open palm, arm outstretched; behind his hand, the hazy outline of Devagiri’s hill and the glinting line of the Arabian Sea frame the horizon.

dialogue.text: Today, that small coin recalls a larger truth: that beyond battles and kings, it was the quiet grind of trade between plateau and coast that made the Yadava hill-fort strong and, in the end, worth conquering.

i18n.hi: आज यह छोटा सिक्का एक बड़ी सच्चाई याद दिलाता है – कि लड़ाइयों और राजाओं से परे, पठार और तट के बीच चलने वाला शांत, रोज़मर्रा का सौदा ही यादवों के पहाड़ी किले को मज़बूत बनाता था, और आख़िर में उसे जीतने लायक भी।

title_i18n.en: The Sea Road and the Silver Coin
title_i18n.hi: समुद्री राह और चाँदी का सिक्का

subtitle_i18n.en: How horses, cotton and a god-marked coin tied a hill kingdom to the sea
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे घोड़े, कपास और देव-चिह्न वाला सिक्का ने पहाड़ी राज्य को सागर से जोड़ा
